name: floti-agents
instructions: These tools start agents of your own, list them and stop them. agents_roles lists the roles an agent can be started in; agents_start runs a new agent in one of them on a task you give it and answers with its name; agents_list shows the agents you started and how many more you may start; agents_stop ends one of them and any it started. They reach only the agents you started: a name that is not one of yours is not found, no tool takes a session id, and none returns any part of a conversation.

tools.name: agents_start
tools.description: Start an agent of your own on a task. It is a full session that runs in the background with the task as its opening prompt, in your folder unless you name another that Floti tracks, and never with more permission than you have. Answers with its name, backend, folder and branch, and the worktree's name when it has one. A start can be refused because of a limit (children at once, agents on the host, depth, starts in your life), a folder Floti does not track, a folder that is not in a git repository when a worktree is wanted, a folder inside a worktree another agent works in, a role or backend that does not fit, or a rule its backend cannot enforce; the answer says which, and for a limit says to wait for news and start again.

task.description: What the agent is to do. It is the agent's opening prompt, so write it as a complete brief.

role.description: The role the agent has, which says which backends may run it, how much it may do on its own and what it is called. Omit it for the default role, agent.

backend.description: The backend to run it on, one the role lists that is installed here. Omit it to use the first the role lists that is installed.

folder.description: The folder it works in, inside a project, harness or profile folder Floti tracks. Omit it to use your own folder.

profile.description: The name of the profile it runs under. Omit it for the role's profile, else the one whose folder holds its folder.

name.description: What you call it. Omit it to use its role's name. A name you already used gets a number after it.

worktree.description: A one-word name for a git worktree Floti makes for it: it works in <repository>/.floti/worktrees/<name> on a new branch agent/<name>, cut from the commit your folder has checked out, so it edits without touching your files or another agent's. Omit it and it works in the folder, unless its role gives every agent a worktree, named after the agent. A name already taken gets a number after it; the answer names the one made. The worktree stays, with its branch, when the agent ends.

outlive.description: Whether it keeps running if you end. Omit it, or pass false, and it ends when you do.

can_start.description: Whether it may start agents of its own. Omit it to use its role's choice.

tools.name: agents_list
tools.description: The agents you started that are running: each one's name, role, class, backend, state, folder and branch, then what is left of your limits. Only your own agents are listed.

tools.name: agents_stop
tools.description: End one of your agents and every agent it started. Pass the name agents_start answered with. A name that is not one of your running agents is not found.

child.description: The name of the agent to end.

tools.name: agents_roles
tools.description: The roles you can start an agent in, read fresh on every call: each one's name, what it is for, its class (light or heavy), whether it works in a worktree of its own, whether its agents may start agents, and the installed backends it can run on for you. Then any role file that cannot be used and what is wrong with it.
